summary: Relocated the plugin's persisted state root outside Jellyfin's PluginsPath so the supported versioned install layout is not deleted on restart once state exists, added a regression test for the versioned-install-plus-state case, and re-ran the live install/upgrade/reload/uninstall verification; Phase 7 acceptance criterion 2 is now met. Chosen state path: Path.Combine(IApplicationPaths.ProgramDataPath, "ArrTags") (the live host resolves this to /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags, a sibling of /tmp/jf/data/plugins). The Plugin constructor calls the public BasePlugin.SetAttributes(assemblyFilePath, dataFolderPath, version) contract (IPluginAssembly, the method the host loader itself uses) to re-point DataFolderPath; AssemblyFilePath and Version are passed through unchanged. Pinned 12.0.0 contract evidence (shallow clone of jellyfin/jellyfin at revision 6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc): MediaBrowser.Common/Plugins/BasePlugin.cs exposes public SetAttributes/DataFolderPath; BasePluginOfT.cs derives DataFolderPath as Path.Combine(ApplicationPaths.PluginsPath, Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(assemblyFilePath)) with a dead '_<version>' branch (Version is null at construction); Emby.Server.Implementations/AppBase/BaseApplicationPaths.cs defines PluginsPath = ProgramDataPath/plugins and DataPath = ProgramDataPath/data; IApplicationPaths exposes ProgramDataPath, DataPath, PluginsPath, PluginConfigurationsPath, CachePath, TempDirectory, TrickplayPath, BackupPath, and the rest. ProgramDataPath was chosen over DataPath because DataPath is a server-managed area already holding host-owned trickplay/backups data, while a plugin-namespaced sibling of plugins/ is unambiguously plugin-owned. Uninstall cleanup analysis: the pinned host's InstallationManager.UninstallPlugin calls plugin.Instance.OnUninstalling() and then PluginManager.RemovePlugin -> DeletePlugin, which deletes only plugin.Path (the install folder), never DataFolderPath; the Phase 5 assumption that the host deletes the plugin data folder held only for the unversioned layout where the install and data folders were the same directory. Relocation therefore changed cleanup behavior, so Plugin.OnUninstalling now runs the bounded synchronous drain and, only when the drain result IsComplete, deletes its own relocated state root (best-effort, guarded to the ArrTags folder name, never throwing); an incomplete or cancelled drain retains the recovery records. The drain is not weakened. Decision recorded as ADR-014 in docs/decisions.md. Regression tests: tests/ArrTags.Tests/PluginStateLocationTests.cs (4 facts; the two location facts fail against the previous derivation - verified by temporarily disabling the relocation) asserts the data folder is outside PluginsPath, that a versioned install folder plus a real persisted state write creates no same-named PluginsPath/ArrTags folder, that a completed drain removes the state root, and that an incomplete drain retains it; tests/ArrTags.Tests/PluginDiscoveryHostTests.cs (2 host-guarded facts) executes the pinned host's real PluginManager discovery/cleanup code from the host Emby.Server.Implementations.dll and proves the versioned install folder is deleted when state lives at PluginsPath/ArrTags and preserved when the state root comes from the production Plugin (the preservation fact also fails when the relocation is temporarily disabled). Live re-verification on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host (http://127.0.0.1:8096, prefix /tmp/jf, plugins at /tmp/jf/data/plugins): a net10.0 probe referencing the built plugin constructed the real Plugin with the host paths and printed Plugin.DataFolderPath = /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags, then wrote a real versioned state record through the production StateRepository/ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore to /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags/authoritative/artwork-lifecycle-fence/active.json. The rebuilt package was installed as the versioned folder ArrTags_0.1.0.0; restart loaded 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0' with the state present and both the install folder and the state record survived (the task 7.2 A/B/A failure is fixed); a further restart reloaded exactly one instance; a temporary 0.1.0.1 upgrade loaded only the newer version and the host auto-deleted the older folder, after which all temporary version edits were reverted with git checkout -- build.yaml Directory.Build.props and the temporary artifact removed; removing the plugin folder produced zero ArrTags loads, zero ArrTags log lines, no [ERR]/[FTL], and a clean 'Startup complete'. Build 0 warnings / 0 errors; default suite Failed 0, Passed 1219, Skipped 60, Total 1279; host-guarded suite (ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR=/tmp/jf/jellyfin) Failed 0, Passed 1235, Skipped 44, Total 1279. The host was returned to a clean, running state (only the .jellyfin-plugin marker and configurations/ remain under data/plugins; no ArrTags install/data folder and no ArrTags.xml).

known_limitations: The live Plugin.OnUninstalling drain and its state-root cleanup could not be exercised on the pinned host: PluginsController is [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)] and StartupWizardCompleted is false, so DELETE /Plugins/<guid>/<version> returns HTTP 401 and no authenticated uninstall is possible. The live uninstall verification therefore removed the plugin folder manually, which does not invoke OnUninstalling and leaves the relocated state root behind; the explicit cleanup is covered in-process by PluginStateLocationTests (completed-drain removal and incomplete-drain retention) and the pre-existing LifecycleFoundationTests/ArtworkLifecycleTests drain facts. The live host was returned to a clean state by removing the orphaned folder manually.

The plugin did not write state on its own during the live run: with no configured Sonarr/Radarr connection and no media library item, no reconciliation, artwork, or fence work is created on startup, so the state record at the new location was written by a task-owned net10.0 probe that constructed the real production Plugin and used the production StateRepository/ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore. This proves the production state path and the discovery safety, but not a live end-to-end state write by a running plugin.

The host-guarded PluginDiscoveryHostTests facts load the host Emby.Server.Implementations.dll via reflection and require ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR; they skip when it is unset, so the default ./build.sh test run does not exercise the real host discovery code. The unguarded PluginStateLocationTests facts cover the same collision boundary with the NuGet-pinned contract.

V1 has no released installs, so no migration is performed. An unreleased developer install may still have an orphaned empty or stale PluginsPath/ArrTags data folder; while it exists it would still trigger the discovery collision, so it must be deleted once. Released V1 installs never create that folder. This is documented in ADR-014.

An incomplete or cancelled uninstall drain retains the relocated state root (by design, so unresolved artwork can be reconciled), which leaves orphaned state on disk after the plugin is gone; an operator must remove it or a reinstall must reconcile it. The completed-drain path removes it.

No live Sonarr or Radarr instance and no live media library item were available, so provider/matching/artwork flows and the live ImageSaver read-back remain unexercised (a pre-existing Phase 5/7 carry-forward, unchanged by this task).

The state-location decision was validated on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host and the net10.0 contract only; the path derivation and discovery behavior are those of the pinned 12.0.0 revision 6c073e19 and are not claimed for other Jellyfin versions.
